title: Transparent usage tiers, pricing guardrails, and overage reconciliation PRD
creator: Ava Chen
summary: Define and deliver a clear, testable pricing layer that exposes transparent usage tiers, hard and soft guardrails for rate limits/quotas, and deterministic overage reconciliation logic for invoices. The PRD covers acceptance criteria, migration strategies for existing customers, telemetry requirements, and key edge-case handling (clock drift, partial-day plan changes, refunds).
background: Customer support and sales have reported repeated confusion about how soft burst credits, hard quotas, and per-route rate-limits interact when customers exceed committed usage. Engineering telemetry shows multiple cases where customers saw unexpected overage charges due to race conditions during plan changes and ambiguous billing windows. We need a single source of truth: explicit rules for quota enforcement, credit consumption order, rounding/proration, and reconciliation flows that can be validated by unit/integration tests and reflected in Console invoices and usage UI.
goals: Publish unambiguous definitions for rate limits (per-minute), quotas (daily/monthly units), and soft burst credit consumption order
Implement deterministic enforcement so identical request sequences produce the same billing outcome in test harnesses
Provide a migration path for existing accounts with soft burst credits so they are not unexpectedly charged
Surface billing calculation breakdown in Console (per-route token cost, credits consumed, overage charges) and expose reconciliation logs for support
Reduce billing-related support tickets by 40% in the first 3 months post-launch
non_goals: Overhaul pricing tiers or introduce new SKUs in this scope
Real-time refunds or automated customer crediting beyond the designed reconciliation window
Implement new third-party billing provider integrations (handled by separate project)
detailed_requirements: Definitions: define 'hard quota' (blocks traffic past limit), 'soft quota' (allows burst consuming credits), 'burst credits' (timebound buffer) and 'overage window' (billing granularity) in a spec page
Quota enforcement: implement enforcement at authorization layer with outcome labels: ALLOW, SOFT_CONSUME, DENY, FALLBACK; log decision with request_id and snapshot of remaining credits
Ordering rules: when a request with multiple routes/tokens is billed, consume credits in this order: per-route credits -> plan credits -> shared pool -> overage (per-unit price)

Partial-day plan change: when a customer upgrades/downgrades mid-billing-window, prorate quotas and credits based on timestamped change; ensure deterministic rounding policy (round up to nearest whole token for quota allocation)
Refund/reconciliation policy: define a 72-hour reconciliation window where anomalies flagged by monitors generate draft invoice adjustments; reconcile with support before final invoice generation
Rate limits (per-caller): implement both global per-caller QPS and per-route per-caller minute limits; soft bursts allowed up to X% for up to Y seconds configurable per plan

Visibility: Console must show per-invoice line items linking to the decision logs for each overage line (request_id list with sampling for large events), and an API to fetch reconciliation logs for automated billing exports
Analytics: emit metrics for: chargeable_units_consumed, credits_consumed_by_type, quota_denials, overage_charge_amount, proration_adjustments
Testing: provide deterministic simulation harness that replays recorded request sets against the pricing engine to validate identical invoice output across environments
acceptance_criteria: Specification published in Confluence with unambiguous terms and examples for five common scenarios (normal usage, sustained burst, mid-window upgrade, shared-pool exhaustion, clock-drift event)
Automated unit and integration tests added that cover: credit ordering, partial-day proration, race between quota update and request, and invoice rounding; tests must run in CI and pass
Billing API returns breakdown for a sample invoice (test account) showing per-route token counts, credits consumed (by bucket), overage lines, and reconciliation flags
Console UI surfaces a per-invoice 'billing trace' that links to stored decision logs for at least 90% of billed requests for a given invoice (sampling allowed for invoices >10k requests)

Support playbook created and validated by SRE and Billing Ops that includes steps for: investigating disputed charges, triggering manual adjustments within the 72-hour window, and escalating to finance
Telemetry: dashboards for the new metrics available in Grafana with alert thresholds (e.g., unexplained proration >0.5% of revenue) configured
Migration: 95% of pilot accounts migrated with automated credit translation scripts and no unplanned overage charge incidents
Performance: pricing decision latency added to request path remains <5ms P95 under nominal load and <20ms P95 under burst tests
Security: all stored billing decision logs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled; audit log exists for manual adjustments
migration_strategy: Two-phased migration. Phase 1 (pilot): choose 10 customers across plan sizes; run in parallel mode (new pricing engine calculates but does not bill) for 1 billing window. Collect diff reports, reconcile with finance, update translation scripts for their soft-burst credit mapping. Phase 2 (opt-in beta): enable billing for beta cohort; monitor reconciliation window closely (72 hours); roll forward to opt-out migration after 2 successful billing cycles. For customers with manual contracts, provide custom mapping and pre-billing review. All migrations are timestamped; a rollback path writes a 'billing-override' event to preserve legacy behavior for a customer for up to one billing cycle.
rollout_plan: Week 0: spec review and sign-off (PM, Eng, Finance, Support). Week 1-3: implementation of enforcement and logs. Week 4: add telemetry/dashboards and console hooks. Week 5: internal integration tests and pilot onboarding. Week 6: pilot billing window in parallel mode. Week 7-8: address pilot issues, finalize scripts. Week 9: open beta for up to 200 customers. Week 12: GA release with communications and updated TOS. Rollback criteria defined: >2 material reconciliation incidents affecting pilot customers or >$50k unexpected overages in beta cohort.
monitoring_and_metrics: proration_adjustments (sum of adjustments applied in reconciliation window)
qa_notes: Create replay harness datasets representing 6 months of recorded traffic from a mid-market customer; test for deterministic output between legacy and new engines
Simulate clock skew by up to +/- 2 minutes and validate reconciliation logic and proration outcomes
Run chaos tests where quota metadata updates race with request flow to ensure idempotent billing decisions
decisions: Use deterministic rounding: quotas prorated and rounded up to nearest whole token to avoid undercharging; decision approved by Finance 2026-02-18
Expose decision logs for up to 90 days in the Console API (sampling for large volumes). Data retention trade-off discussed with Security and accepted with encryption at rest
Grace period for manual adjustments: 72 hours prior to final invoice generation; agreed with Billing Ops
Soft burst default values: allow 30% of plan monthly quota as temporary buffer for up to 120 seconds unless customer has explicit override

open_questions: Should the shared pool credits be transferable across tenants in an organization or remain per-account? (impact: complexity vs flexibility)
What is the acceptable sampling rate for decision logs when invoices exceed 100k billed requests? (performance/storage trade-off)
Do we permit automated small refunds (<$5) to be issued without manual ops approval? Finance prefers manual for now
